nvitk.transform¶

Geometric transform utilities for 3D/4D clinical imaging.

Submodules:

  • nvitk.transform.isotropy — make an image voxel-isotropic by zooming the anisotropic axis.

  • nvitk.transform.resampling — affine-based voxel resampling between two Image grids.

  • nvitk.transform.rotate — rotate a volume around a spatial axis.

  • nvitk.transform.reorient — permute / flip / match reference or mouse preset.

  • nvitk.transform.swap_axes — swap or permute array axes.

  • nvitk.transform.rotation — detect and correct rigid Z-rotation between image grids.

Package Contents¶

nvitk.transform.isotropy(image: nvitk.types.Image, *, axis: int | None = None, factor: float | None = None, order: int = 1, mode: str = 'nearest', prefilter: bool = True) → nvitk.types.Image¶

Resample image along the anisotropic axis to make voxels isotropic.

Parameters:

  • image – 3D Image carrying a spacing triplet.

  • axis – Explicit axis (0, 1, 2) to resample. When omitted, uses the axis with the largest spacing (i.e. lowest sampling density), matching the legacy BioImaging behavior.

  • factor – Explicit zoom factor on the chosen axis. When omitted, uses max(spacing) / min(spacing).

  • order – Spline interpolation order for ndi.zoom. Use 0 for label masks.

  • mode – Boundary mode ('nearest' by default).

  • prefilter – Passed through to ndi.zoom.

Returns:

A new image with updated data and spacing/affine. Axes/orientation are preserved.

Return type:

Image

nvitk.transform.oblique_slice(vol, *, center_xyz, u_xyz, v_xyz, radius_vox: float, res: int, order: int, mode: str = 'constant', cval: float = 0.0)¶

Sample vol on an oblique plane in voxel coordinates (x,y,z).

Parameters:

  • vol – 3D array (NumPy or CuPy).

  • center_xyz – 3-vectors in voxel coordinates. u and v span the plane.

  • u_xyz – 3-vectors in voxel coordinates. u and v span the plane.

  • v_xyz – 3-vectors in voxel coordinates. u and v span the plane.

  • radius_vox – Half-size of the square plane in voxels.

  • res – Output resolution (res × res).

  • order – Interpolation order (0 for masks, 1 for images).

nvitk.transform.mouse_reorient_volume(image: nvitk.types.Image | Any) → nvitk.types.Image¶

Apply the lab mouse / ANTsPy-gallery axis convention (see MOUSE_TARGET_ORIENTATION).

nvitk.transform.reorient_volume(image: nvitk.types.Image | Any, *, mode: str = 'manual', reference: nvitk.types.Image | Any | None = None, target_orientation: str | None = None, permute_order: str | Sequence[int] | None = None, flip_axes: Sequence[bool] | None = None, reset_affine: bool = False) → nvitk.types.Image¶

Reorient a 3D volume via optional axis permute/flips and target axis codes.

Parameters:

  • image – Input Image (or array coerced via metadata-less Image).

  • mode – manual — permute / flip / target codes from arguments. reference — match reference orientation codes (after optional permute/flips). mouse — preclinical preset: permute (0,2,1) then canonical LAS (AP moves from Z→Y; SI ends on Z), matching the ANTsPy mouse gallery layout.

  • reference – Reference image whose orientation codes are the target when mode='reference'.

  • target_orientation – Three-letter codes (e.g. LAS, RAS). Used in manual mode, and as fallback when reference has no readable affine.

  • permute_order – Spatial axis permutation (e.g. "0,2,1" or (0, 2, 1)).

  • flip_axes – Length-3 booleans for flipping array axes 0/1/2 after permute.

  • reset_affine – If True, after permute/flips assign a fresh canonical affine for target_orientation (use when the header axes do not match anatomy). Forced True for mode='mouse'.

nvitk.transform.resample_to(source: nvitk.types.Image, target: nvitk.types.Image, *, order: int = 0, mode: str = 'constant', cval: float = 0.0, prefilter: bool | None = None) → nvitk.types.Image¶

Resample source onto target’s voxel grid via affine composition.

The mapping is T = inv(target.affine) @ source.affine; scipy’s affine_transform expects the output→input map so we invert it.

Parameters:

  • source – Image whose voxels are resampled.

  • target – Image whose grid (shape + affine) defines the output.

  • order – Spline interpolation order. Use 0 for label/mask data (nearest neighbor) and 1 for intensity data.

  • mode – Boundary handling passed to ndi.affine_transform.

  • cval – Boundary handling passed to ndi.affine_transform.

  • prefilter – Defaults to False when order == 0 and True otherwise.

Returns:

A new image whose data lives on target’s grid and carries target’s affine/spacing/orientation but source’s other metadata.

Return type:

Image

nvitk.transform.rotate_volume(image: nvitk.types.Image | Any, angle_degrees: float, *, axis: int = 2, order: int = 1, reshape: bool = False, mode: str = 'constant', cval: float = 0.0) → nvitk.types.Image | Any¶

Rotate a 2D or 3D image by angle_degrees around axis.

Parameters:

  • image – Image or ndarray-like volume.

  • angle_degrees – Counter-clockwise rotation (degrees) in the plane orthogonal to axis (scipy.ndimage.rotate convention).

  • axis – Axis to rotate around for 3D data (0, 1, or 2; default Z). Ignored for 2D (always in-plane).

  • order – Spline interpolation order. Use 0 for label masks.

  • reshape – If True, expand the canvas to fit the rotated content (affine is left unchanged). If False (default), keep the original shape and update the affine when present.

  • mode – Boundary fill for scipy.ndimage.rotate.

  • cval – Boundary fill for scipy.ndimage.rotate.

nvitk.transform.check_and_correct_rotation(pet_affine: numpy.ndarray | Any, mri_affine: numpy.ndarray | Any, pet_image: nvitk.types.Image | None = None, *, threshold_deg: float = 5.0) → RotationAnalysis¶

Compare two affines and optionally correct Z-rotation on pet_image.

Uses the normalized-column relative rotation R_mri @ R_pet.T; the Z rotation is the arctan2 of the 2x2 upper-left block. A near-180° reflection case is detected via the signs of R_relative.

Parameters:

  • pet_affine – 4x4 voxel-to-world affines. CuPy arrays are materialized to NumPy.

  • mri_affine – 4x4 voxel-to-world affines. CuPy arrays are materialized to NumPy.

  • pet_image – Optional PET image to correct when rotation exceeds threshold_deg.

  • threshold_deg – Tolerance (degrees) under which correction is skipped.

nvitk.transform.correct_z_rotation(image: nvitk.types.Image | None, affine: numpy.ndarray, rotation_degrees: float)¶

Rotate image and its affine by -rotation_degrees around the Z axis.

Parameters:

  • image – Optional Image to rotate. If None only the affine is updated.

  • affine – 4x4 voxel-to-world affine (NumPy).

  • rotation_degrees – Rotation to undo (the function applies -rotation_degrees). A fast path is used for |180°|.

Returns:

Rotated image (or None) and updated affine.

Return type:

(Image | None, np.ndarray)

nvitk.transform.permute_axes(image: nvitk.types.Image | Any, order: Sequence[int]) → nvitk.types.Image | Any¶

Reorder array axes to order.

Parameters:

  • image – Image or ndarray-like.

  • order – New axis order. Must be a permutation of 0..ndim-1, or of 0..k-1 to permute only the leading k axes (e.g. spatial of 4D).
